| [THEORY-028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md) v2 | The expected bias of any data-dependent choice, and the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm, is at most √(2σ²·I) for σ-subgaussian losses, where I is the information the output carries about the data | Russo & Zou (2015), [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md), Prop. 1: \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) for any selection T among σ-sub-Gaussian statistics. | [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) | The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). Stanislaw & Todorov (1999), [LIT-367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md), state that d′ varies with the criterion unless the variances are equal. The separation of sensitivity from bias is a property of the model, not of the data. | Active |
| [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) | A Markov-blanket partition is defined relative to a chosen internal set, so a graph has one around almost any set of nodes, and the formalism alone does not say which set is the system | The formal core of Bruineberg et al.'s critique ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md), C4 in [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md)). In a directed acyclic graph the blanket of a node set A is its parents, children and the children's other parents, and A is conditionally independent of everything outside A and its blanket. That holds for every A, so any set whose blanket leaves something outside gets a valid internal, blanket and external partition. Having a blanket therefore picks out no set. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the set was picked by spectral clustering with k = 8, not by the blanket. Active because it is a short derivation that anyone can check. It covers graphical (Pearl) blankets and the 2013 procedure. It does not cover the later sparse-coupling definitions at nonequilibrium steady state, which the record has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md) v2 | In a two-alternative choice made by two competing leaky accumulators, the decision is optimal only when leak and mutual inhibition balance, so that the network integrates the difference of the evidence without loss; imbalance bounds accuracy at any fixed time and weights early or late evidence | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) prove that the pure drift diffusion model is the continuum limit of the sequential probability ratio test, and so the optimal two-choice decider, and that the linearised Usher–McClelland network reduces to it exactly when leak equals inhibition (and, for free response, when both are also large). Usher and McClelland ([LIT-565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-565.md)) derived the difference of the two units as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β: K ≠ 0 caps accuracy, leak-dominant weights late evidence and inhibition-dominant early. Active because the core is derivation, checkable on paper. What it does not say: that brains are balanced, that the result carries to more than two options or to non-stationary evidence, or that the primacy and recency seen in six participants are explained by it. | Active |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v2 | In Friston's 2013 formulation and the applications the record holds, a Markov blanket does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is traced (the coupling graph, the internal set and the time at which steady state is assumed), and a blanket read from a fixed graph is the same whether the system produced the boundary or it was imposed | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. ([LIT-598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-598.md)) argue, by different routes, that the Markov blanket of the free-energy literature is placed and not found. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Active since 2026-10-27, narrowed to the 2013 formulation and the applications held. The later steady-state definitions have not been read, and the unrestricted claim is THEORY-1097, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v2 | Bayesian model reduction under the Laplace approximation prices the reductions of a singular parent model with a Gaussian Occam factor, so its free-energy differences can be wrong by a term that grows with log n | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. | [THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md) v2 | The evidence of any model formed from a full model by changing only its prior is the full evidence times the full posterior expectation of the prior ratio, so the Savage–Dickey ratio is its point-mass case and choosing which parameters to keep is evidence maximisation over the prior | Friston & Penny (2011), [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 3: if models share a likelihood and differ only in priors nested inside a full prior, then p(y\|m_i) = p(y\|m_F)·E_{p(θ\|y,m_F)}[p_i(θ)/p_F(θ)]. | [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) v2 | The Bayesian complexity penalty grows as (d/2) log n in a regular model, where the curvature at the optimum sets the Occam factor, and as λ log n in a singular one, where λ is the real log canonical threshold and falls below d/2 when the prior is positive on the optimal set | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. | [THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md) v2 | Iterated learning by Bayesian agents who sample from the posterior converges, in an ergodic chain, to the shared prior | Griffiths & Kalish (2007), [LIT-769](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-769.md), read in [NOTE-599](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md): a chain of learners who share a prior and each sample a hypothesis from their posterior is a Gibbs sampler, so the probability a learner holds a hypothesis converges to its prior probability, whatever the amount of data passed on; with MAP learners the outcome centres on the prior's mode but depends on data amount and noise, and can amplify weak biases. It is a theorem about an idealized chain. It does not say human chains reach the prior, and Kirby, Cornish & Smith's laboratory chains, [LIT-771](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-771.md), are consistent with it without testing it. Whether human chains do is [QUESTION-137](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | The classical theorems on sufficient statistics need only the copy/discard structure of Markov kernels: Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need only strict positivity, not the existence of conditional distributions | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. | [THEORY-158](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md) v2 | For a Markov process on a finite state space, an observable commutes with the generator exactly when its mean and variance are both conserved in every state, which is exactly when it is constant on each connected component of the transition graph, so a conserved mean alone does not give a symmetry | Baez & Fong (2013), [LIT-773](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-773.md), read in [NOTE-598](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-598.md): Theorem 1 (finite state space, four equivalent conditions), which the record re-derived. | [THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md) v3 | In the 66 Pew surveys of 2001–2011 that varied the order of two back-to-back binary questions, question order changed the answers but not the probability of giving the same answer to both, the equality a Lüders projection model predicts for any projectors; a classical model with order events can meet the same equality, so the regularity does not by itself favour quantum over classical probability | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), on the QQ equality derived in [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md): across the 66 Pew surveys of 2001-2011 that varied the order of two questions, question order shifts the answers (p = 0.0004) but not the probability that the two answers agree (p = 0.4625). | [THEORY-215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md) | A Hawkes process with a Lipschitz rate function and signed kernels has a unique stationary regime, which suitably started versions approach, when the Lipschitz-weighted absolute kernel mass is below one (a spectral radius below one, for a network) or when the rate is bounded | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md), read in [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md): Theorems 1, 2, 7 and 8, proved. | [THEORY-247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-247.md) v2 | For finite action-free labelled Markov chains, the discounted bisimulation metric, defined as the unique fixed point of Ferns et al.'s equation, is a bicausal optimal-transport distance, and it equals the value of a finite linear program over occupancy couplings | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2024), [LIT-962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-962.md), read in [NOTE-757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-757.md). | [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) v3 | With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight for every pair of distributions only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus, with Fourier coefficients proportional to e^(−σ‖ω‖₁) and strictly positive Lipschitz densities, is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks | Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md). Σ_p = ∫ϕϕ* dp is uncentred and unit-trace, so p ↦ Σ_p maps distributions to quantum states, and D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q) (Proposition 4(d), Eq. 8). The upper bound is joint convexity, with equality for every pair only if k(x,y) = 0 for x ≠ y. The lower bound is monotonicity under a measurement whose outcome law is p smoothed by h(x,y) = ⟨ϕ(x), Σ^{−1/2}ϕ(y)⟩². | [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) | An ideal observer is optimal relative to the information it is given, so a constrained ideal is the optimal decoder of a degraded input, not a restricted decoder of the full one; comparing real observers with ideals taken at successive stages of the visual system places losses by stage, and in early-vision tasks human performance is reported to parallel the retinal-stage ideal across conditions while falling well below it | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md).
